Several individuals have walked around the Earth (completed pedestrian circumnavigations), with Dave Kunst recognized as the first independently verified person to do so. Because oceans prevent a continuous land journey, walking around the world requires crossing multiple continents on foot and traveling across oceans by boat or plane. Key individuals who achieved this include: Dave Kunst (1970–1974): The first verified person to walk around the world. He walked over 14,400 miles across four continents, starting and finishing in Waseca, Minnesota. Steven M. Newman (1983–1987): The first person recorded to complete a solo walk around the globe, traversing 14,500 miles across 22 countries and four continents. Ffyona Campbell (1985–1994): The first woman to walk across multiple continents—covering North America, Australia, Africa, and Europe—totaling roughly 20,000 miles. George Meegan (1977–1983): Set the record for the longest unbroken continuous walk in history, traveling 19,019 miles from the southern tip of Argentina to the northern coast of Alaska. Jean Béliveau (2000–2011): Walked 46,600 miles (75,000 km) across 64 countries over 11 years to promote peace and non-violence for children. Karl Bushby (1998–2026): Completed the Goliath Expedition, an unbroken 36,000-mile foot journey from Chile to England. Notably, he walked from South America up through North America, crossed the frozen Bering Strait on foot into Russia, and walked through Asia and Europe back home.

anyways here’S A cookie recipe Prep time: 20 mins (+ at least 2 hours chilling time) Bake time: 10–12 minutes Yields: About 12 large bakery-style cookies ingredients: - 1 cup (226g) unsalted butter (browned for extra depth) - 1 cup (200g) dark brown sugar, packed (for moisture and chewiness) - ½ cup (100g) granulated white sugar (for crisp edges) - 2 large eggs (room temperature) - 2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract - 3 cups (360g) all-purpose flour - 1 teaspoon baking soda - ¾ teaspoon fine sea salt - 1 ½ cups (250g) bittersweet or semisweet chocolate (a mix of chopped bars and chips creates the best puddles) - Flaky sea salt (for finishing) instructions: 1. Brown the Butter: - Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, swirling occasionally. - It will melt, foam, and then start crackling. After 3 to 5 minutes, the crackling will stop, and foam will rise again. Watch closely: brown specks will appear at the bottom of the pan, and it will smell deeply nutty. - Immediately remove from heat and pour it into a large mixing bowl. Stir in a couple of ice cubes or 2 tablespoons of cold water to quickly cool it down and replenish evaporated moisture. Let it cool until warm (not hot). 2. Mix the Wet Ingredients: - Add both the brown sugar and white sugar to the warm browned butter. Whisk vigorously for about 1 minute until well combined and slightly pale. - Add the eggs one at a time, whisking well after each. - Whisk in the vanilla extract until the mixture becomes smooth and glossy. 3. Fold in the Dry Ingredients: - Switch to a rubber spatula. Add the flour, baking soda, and fine sea salt. - Fold gently just until streaks of flour disappear. Do not overmix. - Fold in your chocolate chunks and chips, making sure they are evenly distributed. 4. The Crucial Chill: - Cover the bowl tightly and chill the dough in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours (overnight is even better). 5. Bake to Perfection: - Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper. - Scoop large balls of dough (about 3 tablespoons / 75g each) and place them at least 3 inches apart on the sheet. - Bake for 10 to 12 minutes. The edges should be golden brown and set, but the centers should still look slightly soft and underbaked. - Halfway through or right as they come out of the oven, gently tap the baking sheet on the counter once or twice to deflate the cookies slightly for rippled chewy edges. 6. Finish and Serve: - Sprinkle a tiny pinch of flaky sea salt over the hot cookies immediately as they come out of the oven. - Let them cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack.
